column1: # Existing oversized Swift files. Each entry ratchets its current counts downward
# until it reaches the defaults: 800 lines / 12 top-level types / 400 lines in the
# 2026-09-25, file-size split: the gate had been red at HEAD with 87 rows over
# (committed and uncommitted growth since the rows were last written). Every
# one was brought under its row by pure code motion, not by raising the row:
# declarations moved into `<File>+<Topic>.swift` siblings or same-file
# `extension` blocks, bodies untouched, `private` relaxed only where a move
# crossed a file. Rows were then lowered to the new counts (78 rows), and the
# 12 rows whose files now meet the 800 / 12 / 400 defaults were dropped.
# 2026-09-28, file-size split after the UI polish pass: ~50 files had grown
# past their rows (plus a dozen more that a concurrent copy-rewrite session grew
# while this pass ran). All but four were brought back under by pure code
# motion into new sibling files (no `+` in names) or same-file `extension`
# splits, bodies untouched, `private` relaxed only where a move crossed a file;
# touched rows were lowered to the new counts and rows now under the defaults
# dropped. Four rows are raised or added because no pure move can shrink them:
#                                it is the file's only declaration.
#   LifeThreadComposerHost       `host(router:)` is one 416-line function; it now
#                                sits alone in its own extension (446 -> 423).
#   ChatScaffoldView / AdaptiveHome  the struct is stored properties (+ init) plus
#                                `body`. `body` cannot leave the struct by motion
#                                alone: in an extension it loses the protocol's
#                                moving AdaptiveHome's init out would synthesize
# Shrinking these needs section extraction inside a body, which is a refactor.
# 2026-08-10, UI polish: two rows grew by exactly one line each, deliberately.
# Track's root ScrollView and AdaptiveHome each gained
# capsule/orb compression. Neither file can shrink to pay for it without a
# separate extraction pass, and blocking a one-line modifier behind a 4,500-line
# refactor is how a ratchet stops being useful. Every other file in this change
# was brought under the limit by extraction instead — see LifeThreadComposerHost,
# whose largest declaration went 436 -> under 400 by moving `host(router:)` and
# 2026-08-10, signal rings restored: Gallery 5028 -> 5017 (ratcheted DOWN; the
# SignalStrip adoption was reverted at the user's request and `ring(_:)` came
# back smaller than the strip plumbing it replaced). AtmosphereRenderer
# separates "HealthKit was never authorized" from "authorized, nothing recorded
# yet" — the mapping used to collapse both into a dashed "+", which promised
# that tapping would let you add a value a permission gate cannot accept.
# 'largest' is the metric that predicts the -Onone launch crash: Debug inlines a
# computed 'some View' property into its caller's frame, so it is the size of the
# TYPE, not the file, that overflows the 1 MB main stack. Extracting a section into
# a sibling struct therefore shows up here as progress even though the file grows.
# 2026-08-07 regenerated after the parallel -Onone split pass. File 'lines' grew for
# ChatView / WeeklyPlanningWorkspaceView / LifeOSFoundationShell because extracting a
# section into a sibling struct adds declarations; 'largest' is the column that matters
# and it fell sharply. The later structural wave landed the AdaptiveHome split.

# `validate(start:end:)` calls, fixing an intermittent SIGSEGV where a malformed date
# bound reached HealthKit's predicate description and faulted in __dtoa. A crash fix,
# 2026-08-08: three rows gained 3-6 lines when the Home shrapnel was
# consolidated — each file picked up a header explaining why it is kept
# separate. The type sizes (603, 402, 409) are unchanged, which is the
# number this ratchet exists to drive down.

# reference removed. Type sizes are unchanged except where the property

# fasting deep links grew nine rows. LifeBoardPhaseVIViews was measured mid-
# extraction (1558) and landed at 2410 once the WellnessView/NutritionView

# views, the acknowledged-leaf navigation protocol, and resolved Home card

# 2026-08-11, eva composer clearance: bridged composer focus state added six
# lines to ChatView and moved the chat's prompt field into the structured
# composer (+10 lines to its single top-level declaration). Type sizes are
# unchanged in the file that matters (ChatView's largest type held at 424;
# 2026-08-22, shader readiness observed: every signature-effect modifier gated
# itself on `SignatureShaders.isReadyForRendering`, a plain `static var` read
# inside its own body. That read is not observation-tracked, and warm-up is a
# detached Task, so the first render of each effect took its fallback branch and
# was never invalidated when the shaders became ready — almost no Metal effect
# in the app was reaching the screen. The fix is one
# declaration lines plus the rule documented at the definition site. The
# largest-type column is unchanged at 145, so the -Onone launch-stack budget
# this ratchet exists to protect is untouched; the growth is declaration count.
# 2026-09-24, keyboard contract: SunriseEvaSheets +12. The Focus timer's
# "Custom minutes" was a number pad in a half-height sheet with no Return, no
# Done and nothing to scroll — its keyboard could only be put away by starting
# or closing. It is a `ValueDrum` now, and Start is pinned in a bottom inset so
# the taller drum cannot push it off a small phone at the medium detent. The
# largest-type column is unchanged at 307; the growth is the sheet's own struct.
